subject: sarf
definition: A noun derived from a verb for the one who does the act, such as nāṣir (helper) from naṣara.
explanation: From the bare verb it is on the pattern فَاعِلٌ: نَاصِرٌ، ضَارِبٌ، كَاتِبٌ. From the added patterns it is the present tense with mīm and ḍamma in place of the prefix, and a kasra before the last letter: مُكْرِمٌ (one who honours), مُسْتَغْفِرٌ (one who asks forgiveness).
It can work like its verb: in زَيْدٌ ضَارِبٌ عَمْرًا (Zayd is striking ʿAmr), ʿAmr is manṣūb as the object of ḍārib.

examples.english: muʿallimun, one who teaches, from ʿallama.
